body: See my comment here https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/12305#issuecomment-4114487190 which I think applies to this issue also.

So, the answer to "does opening a hint close a sibling auto popover?" is 'sometimes', and that's fully intentional? I cannot think of a case where this behaviour is beneficial, yet it's a gotcha in simple multi-level menus.

I don't think this is a documentation issue. I think the requirements got confused along the way, or the requirements were incorrectly spec'd.

Are you around for this week's WHATNOT meeting?

> But the spec and behavior were extensively discussed. Please read the hundreds of comments (each) on the issue and PR:
> 
> * [popover=hint #9776](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9776)
> * [Add popover=hint #9778](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/9778)

I can't find any discussion around making the behaviour I documented in this issue intentional, or why it would be desirable. I did find https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9776#issuecomment-1834130914:

> Hearing nothing, I'm going to assume that means there are no objections to this new direction.

…Which smells like a lot of changes didn't receive proper review.

Edit: moved proposed 'spec' to a later comment.

The goal IMO should be:

- Opening an `auto` popover closes all `auto` & `hint` popovers except those that are ancestors.
- Opening a `hint` popover closes all `hint` popovers except those that are ancestors.

This feels fairly simple to explain to developers compared to whatever the current behaviour is.

I looked at all the videos and to me the current behavior looks inconsistently weird indeed.

> The goal here is that:
> 
> * Opening an `auto` popover closes all `auto` & `hint` popovers except those that are ancestors.
> * Opening a `hint` popover closes all `hint` popovers except those that are ancestors.
> 
> This feels fairly simple to explain to developers compared to whatever the current behaviour is.

This seems like a reasonable model that I could wrap my head around.

One question though: when you say “close all [X] popovers except those that are ancestors” you mean that the popovers themselves are nested? Knowing that popovers can live anywhere in the DOM, the “nested” ones could just be sibling elements. Therefore it might be better to base yourself on the triggering element that shows the nested popover. As in: Close all [X] popovers except for the popover that contains the triggering source element that shows the new popover. The wording here might need some tweaking to more clearly convey the message and to play nice with multiple levels of popovers.
Yeah, you're right. I don't have the opener logic in there. I deleted my shitty spec. Here's a less shitty one…

Assuming that hint popovers are intended for hover tooltip style things, here's a set of behaviours that I think make sense: - Nesting an `auto` popover within a `hint` popover is weird. We should either prevent this from happening, or treat that `auto` popover as a `hint` popover for the rest of this ruleset. - A popover's parent is the open popover closest to a popover's the invoking button (at open time) or the popover element itself (at open time), whichever appears first in the `auto`+`hint` stack. - Opening an `auto` popover will close other `auto` popovers, except its ancestor popovers. - Opening an `auto` popover will close all `hint` popovers (unless it's nested in a `hint` popover, in which case it's a failure or we treat it as a `hint` popover) - Opening a `hint` popover will close other `hint` popovers, except its ancestor popovers. - Opening a `hint` popover will not close `auto` popovers. - Closing a `hint` popover will also close 'child' `hint` popovers. - Closing an `auto` popover will also close 'child' `hint` & `auto` popovers. It will not close other popovers (including `hint`). This allows an `auto` popover to be closed on a timeout without impacting tooltip `hint` popovers. - Clicking will hide `auto` & `hint` popovers, except any popover that contains the clicked item, and its parent popovers. - `manual` popovers continue to operate independently. Closing/opening one does not impact `auto`/`hint` popovers. Here's a pseudo-spec proposal: ## Infra - The `autoRootedPopoverStack` is a stack of open popovers in the `auto` state. - The `hintRootedPopoverStack` is a stack of open popovers in the `hint` or `auto` state. > This will only contain `auto` popovers if we allow `auto` popovers 'inside' `hint` popovers. We can choose not to allow that. I've included both options below. These stacks can be 'getters' the operate on the top-layer. - The `hintStackParent` is an open popover in the `auto` state, or null. Initially null. > If the hints are nested inside an `auto` popover, this property tracks their start point. It's effectively a 'branch' off the auto stack. This is useful when hiding popovers, as we can determine if hiding an `auto` popover should also hide the hints. Some diagrams of potential states: ## When a `popoverToOpen` (HTMLElement) is to be opened via `source` (HTMLElement or null): 1. If `popoverToOpen` is in the `manual` state, then just open it and return. 1. Let `popoverToOpenParent` be the topmost popover ancestor of `popoverToOpen` and `source` (algorithm below). 1. While `hintRootedPopoverStack` is not empty: > We hide `hint` popovers first, as new `auto` and `hint` popovers should hide existing `hint` popovers, except in the nested case. 1. Let `popover` be the last item in `hintRootedPopoverStack`. 1. If `popoverToOpenParent` is `popover`, then: 1. **Option A:** If `popoverToOpen` is in the `auto` state, then throw an error indicating that an `auto` popover cannot be opened inside a `hint` popover. **Option B:** Otherwise, we continue, and `popoverToOpen` is effectively shown as a `hint` popover. 1. Push `popoverToOpen` onto `hintRootedPopoverStack`. 1. Show `popoverToOpen` and return. 1. Hide `popover`. 1. Pop `hintRootedPopoverStack`. 1. Set `hintStackParent` to null. 1. If `popoverToOpen` is in the `auto` state, then: 1. While `autoRootedPopoverStack` is not empty: > Since this is an `auto` popover, it will hide existing `auto` popovers, except in the nested case. 1. Let `popover` be the last item in `autoRootedPopoverStack`. 1. If `popoverToOpenParent` is `popover`, then break. 1. Hide `popover`. 1. Pop `autoRootedPopoverStack`. 1. Push `popoverToOpen` onto `autoRootedPopoverStack`. 1. Show `popoverToOpen` and return. 1. Otherwise (`popoverToOpen` is in the `hint` state): 1. Assert: `hintRootedPopoverStack` is empty. > This is a new 'branch' of `hint` popovers. 1. Push `popoverToOpen` onto `hintRootedPopoverStack`. 1. If `popoverToOpenParent` is not null, then: 1. Assert: `popoverToOpenParent` is in the `auto` state. 1. Set `hintStackParent` to `popoverToOpenParent`. 1. Show `popoverToOpen` and return. ## To get the topmost popover ancestor of `popover` (HTMLElement) and source (HTMLElement or null): 1. Let `allPopovers` be a list that's a concatenation of `autoRootedPopoverStack` and `hintRootedPopoverStack`. 1. Let `popoverAncestorIndex` be the index of the last item in `allPopovers` whose flattened tree contains `popover`, otherwise infinity. 1. Let `sourceAncestorIndex` be infinity. 1. If `source` is not null, then set `sourceAncestorIndex` to the index of the last item in `allPopovers` whose flattened tree contains `source`, otherwise infinity. 1. Let `ancestorIndex` be the minimum of `popoverAncestorIndex` and `sourceAncestorIndex`. 1. If `ancestorIndex` is infinity, then return null, otherwise return `allPopovers[ancestorIndex]`. ## To hide `popoverToHide` (HTMLElement): > In the current spec, if you hide any `auto` popover, then _all_ `hint` popovers are also hidden. This seems unnecessary, but I guess we could keep it that way. That isn't what I've done here though. Here, if an `auto` popover is hidden, it only hides `hint` popovers if the hints are rooted at one of the closed popovers. > > This means, for example, if you have an auto popover that you hide on a timeout, it won't cause unrelated hints to also close. 1. If `popoverToHide` is in the `manual` state, then just hide it and return. 1. If `hintRootedPopoverStack` contains `popoverToHide`, then: 1. While true: 1. Let `popover` be the last item in `hintRootedPopoverStack`. 1. Hide `popover`. 1. Pop `hintRootedPopoverStack`. 1. If `popover` is `popoverToHide`, then return. 1. Let `autoStackIndex` be the index of `popoverToHide` in `autoRootedPopoverStack`, otherwise -1. 1. Assert: `autoStackIndex` is not -1. 1. Let `autoPopoversToHide` be the slice of `autoRootedPopoverStack` from `autoStackIndex` to the end. 1. If `autoPopoversToHide` contains `hintStackParent`, then: > This is the case where we're hiding an `auto` popover that's the root of the `hint` stack, so we need to hide all `hint` popovers as well. 1. While `hintRootedPopoverStack` is not empty: 1. Let `popover` be the last item in `hintRootedPopoverStack`. 1. Hide `popover`. 1. Pop `hintRootedPopoverStack`. 1. Set `hintStackParent` to null. 1. While true: 1. Let `popover` be the last item in `autoRootedPopoverStack`. 1. Hide `popover`. 1. Pop `autoRootedPopoverStack`. 1. If `popover` is `popoverToHide`, then return. ## On click 1. Let `parentPopoverOrNull` be the closest `hint` or `auto` popover to the clicked element, otherwise null. 1. While `hintRootedPopoverStack` is not empty: 1. Let `popover` be the last item in `hintRootedPopoverStack`. 1. If `parentPopoverOrNull` is `popover`, then break. 1. Hide `popover`. 1. Pop `hintRootedPopoverStack`. 1. If `hintRootedPopoverStack` is empty, then set `hintStackParent` to null. 1. While `autoRootedPopoverStack` is not empty: 1. Let `popover` be the last item in `autoRootedPopoverStack`. 1. If `parentPopoverOrNull` is `popover` or `parentPopoverOrNull` is `hintStackParent`, then return. > `hintStackParent` prevents the 'parent' `auto` of a clicked `hint` popover being hidden. 1. Hide `popover`. 1. Pop `autoRootedPopoverStack`. --- If we went with this model: **Weirdness 1 - solved.** Opening the `hint` popover would not close the sibling `auto` popover, as closing items in the `auto` stack is something only `auto` popovers can do (step 4). This makes it consistent with the non-nested popover behaviour. **Weirdness 2 - solved.** Because the nested `hint` popover is in the `hint` stack (unlike the current spec that puts it in the `auto` stack), then only one `hint` popover would be shown at a time, as the other(s) are hidden as part of step 3. The only case where multiple hint popovers can be shown is when they're nested (step 3.ii). **Weirdness 3 - solved.** On click, if a `hint` popover is cleared, unrelated `auto` popovers are also closed. **Weirdness 4 - solved.** When a popover hides, it only hides its 'children' popovers, not all popovers. **Weirdness 5 - two options.** Opening the `auto` popover inside the `hint` popover would not hide the `hint` popover, as it's an ancestor (step 3.ii). As per step 3.ii.a, it would either throw at this point (since you can't put `auto` popovers in `hint` popovers), or it allows it by treating it as a `hint` popover, and putting it in the `hint` stack. All of these feel way more intuitive than what currently happens, but I assume this model breaks some other use-cases? What are they?

Summary of the weird behaviours with the current model (but there may be more):

- Unnested, opening an `auto` popover then a `hint` popover shows both. Nested, opening an `auto` popover then a `hint` popover hides the `auto` popover. The nested behaviour seems wrong.
- Opening a nested `hint` popover then an unnested `hint` popover shows both hints. Opening an unnested `hint` popover then a nested `hint` popover hides the first. Unless nested within each other, only one hint should be shown at a time.
- Opening an unnested `auto` popover and an unnested `hint` popover, then clicking within the `hint` popover, leaves both popovers visible, even though the `auto` popover is unrelated to the `hint`. Clicking outside an `auto` or `hint` popover should close it.
- Opening an `auto` popover within a `hint` popover leaves things in a broken state. Apparently you "can't" do this, but the only web-standard source of that rule is [the name of this test](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/html/semantics/popovers/popover-types-with-hints.html#L111). If this shouldn't be allowed, we should prevent it happening, or find some non-broken way for it to happen.

All of these are addressed by my proposal above.

Without having read the full comments here, here's my thoughts.

TLDR I agree each of those cases feels unintuative to authors.

## Weirdness 1 :

That’s definitely not desirable imo, the whole point of hint is that it should not close auto popovers, the fact they’re nested inside of an auto popover should not change that.

## Weirdness 2:

That also feels very strange, like you say a world in which nested hints don’t close root ones, could make sense but in that case opening the root one *shouldn’t* close the nested ones.  I think I would prefer if a hint just always closes non-ancestor hints. But the current behaviour is wrong imo.

## Weirdness 3:

I wonder what the spec reason for that is? I could be persuaded that maybe this is desirable behaviour to able to copy text out of a tooltip or something, but it doesn’t immediately feel like it should be the behaviour based on my understanding of the spec.

## Weirdness 4:
I get that showing an auto does close hints but I don’t know that *closing* an auto should have any impact on hints (other than descendants).

## Weirdness 5

We should probably just make showPopover/togglePopover throw when the source is inside a hint popover. (Likewise popovertarget/commandfor would just do nothing). I agree this isn’t something that feels useful but it also shouldn’t be broken like this.

So generally I think I need more time to work through all of the weirdness examples here. However, it feels like at least a few of them, and perhaps all of them (?) are due to how `display:none` works, and really nothing to do with popover logic. I mentioned a bit of that in this comment: https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/12305#issuecomment-4113098373. It would be super helpful to disambiguate that from any other issues. I.e. I believe in the OP here you're using the word "close" to mean two different things, in different cases. In one case, you mean the ["hide popover algorithm"](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#hide-popover-algorithm) is run on a popover, and in others, you mean that a parent element in the layout tree has `display:none` and therefore the popover element is not rendered. I'm not sure we can/should try to solve the second issue, since it's a lot bigger than just popovers, as shown in the comment I just linked above.

> So, the answer to "does opening a hint close a sibling auto popover?" is 'sometimes', and that's fully intentional? I cannot think of a case where this behaviour is beneficial, yet it's a gotcha in simple multi-level menus.

The answer to this should be "never". Hints are subordinate to autos, so opening a hint shouldn't [close](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#hide-popover-algorithm) an auto. The ["hide all popovers until" algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#hide-all-popovers-until) should encode this behavior. Step 8 should keep a `hint` popover from closing any `auto` popovers.

I'm still paging back in all of these discussions from 2-3 years ago, but this paragraph of the explainer attempts to capture the logic of the existing stack: [Popover Stacks](https://open-ui.org/components/popover-hint.research.explainer/#proposal-popoverhint:~:text=Further%2C%20it%20should,popover%3Dauto).

> However, it feels like at least a few of them, and perhaps all of them (?) are due to how `display:none` works

I don't think any of them are related to this. "Weirdness 5" has some side-effect because of `display:none`, but https://random-stuff.jakearchibald.com/popover-hint-flat/ here are the same demos but without nesting the popover elements themselves, and the behaviour is still weird/broken.

> > So, the answer to "does opening a hint close a sibling auto popover?" is 'sometimes', and that's fully intentional? I cannot think of a case where this behaviour is beneficial, yet it's a gotcha in simple multi-level menus.
> 
> The answer to this should be "never". Hints are subordinate to autos, so opening a hint shouldn't [close](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#hide-popover-algorithm) an auto. The ["hide all popovers until" algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#hide-all-popovers-until) should encode this behavior.

I agree the answer should be "never", but the spec currently says otherwise.

[Here is where it happens in the spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-popover-attribute:opened-in-popover-mode-2:~:text=then%3A-,Run%20hide,auto%22%2E), and [here's a test for it](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/5f2701d054546b9e5ee5c77244af1e9ae3b1f65b/html/semantics/popovers/popover-types-with-hints.html#L128).

(Edit: This is about **weirdness #1**.) > [Here is where it happens in the spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-popover-attribute:opened-in-popover-mode-2:~:text=then%3A-,Run%20hide,auto%22%2E), and [here's a test for it](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/5f2701d054546b9e5ee5c77244af1e9ae3b1f65b/html/semantics/popovers/popover-types-with-hints.html#L128). Oh, thanks for linking (twice!) to that test. It made me realize at least part of what's going on there. That does make sense doesn't it? I.e. here's the situation: ```mermaid graph BT A[auto 1] --> B[auto 2] A[auto 1] --> C[hint 3] ``` Both of the top popovers are "nested" (in [the popover sense](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#topmost-popover-ancestor)) inside the bottom one. Opening one sibling closes the other, in either direction. An real-world-ish example of that would be a top level menu (auto 1) that can open sub-menus (auto 2). But it also has a hovercard/tooltip (hint 3) related to the top level menu (auto 1). Showing hint 3 hides auto 2, because the hovercard is about the parent menu. This is a bit convoluted, but it was constructed this way by the developer, so perhaps they know best? I'd love to attach use case "names" to each of the "weirdnesses", so at least I can think about how the model doesn't serve those use cases. The current behavior is very much informed by a set of use cases (e.g. hover cards, tooltips, select pickers, menus, etc.) and perhaps there are some missing ones. If we're just enumerating weirdnesses, we could do that for a while. I'm guessing you constructed these examples while trying to build something real - mind helping me understand each of the use cases a bit better? In the meantime, I'm going to work my way through the 5 examples, and see if I can wrap my head around what's going on in each.

Ok, I've now had a chance to go through the rest. Thanks for the videos with sound - that was *super* helpful. (Other than having to unmute each one and then rewind to hear the beginning. 😄 ) **Weirdness #2**: ```mermaid graph BT A[auto 1] --> B[hint 2] A[auto 1] --> C[hint 3] D[hint 4] ``` The "weirdness" here is that the related, nested hints 2 and 3 close each other, while the unrelated, non-nested hint 4 can be opened while leaving one of 2 or 3 open. Again, this comes from an example use case. Let's say auto 1 is a select popover with options. And hint 2 and 3 are tooltips related to some content within one of the options, perhaps explaining more detail about the full name or email address in an email address picker, for example. Showing one of them closes the other, quite naturally. And let's say hint 4 is a tooltip for an unrelated item somewhere else on the page, perhaps a tooltip on the "send email" button. Hovering to show that unrelated tooltip shouldn't close either the (auto) picker or the (hint) tooltip on the picker. **Weirdness #3** Here, I think the behavior is correct. A use case is that you have a picker open to fill in some information (e.g. someone's name), and you hover that persons username on the page to show the hovercard about them, and you want to copy/paste from the hovercard into the auto popover. Since it opened "second" it can stay open while you interact with it. The algorithms essentially behave as if the entire hint stack sits "on top" of the auto stack. So since you're clicking inside the hint, both stacks get to stay open while you interact with the topmost thing, the hint popover. This is very much analogous to having straight nested `auto` popovers: ```mermaid graph BT A[auto 1] --> B[auto 2] ``` If you click inside auto 2, it does not light dismiss auto 1, because it's on top. **Weirdness #4** This is again (like weirdness 3) because the hint stack is "on top of" the auto stack. In your example, you've opened an auto, then opened a hint, then hidden the auto. That hides the hint stack also. A concrete example would be that you've opened a select picker, then hovered something to get a tooltip. Closing the picker "wipes the slate" and closes everything. *Usually* hiding the picker happens because the user clicked outside to light dismiss it, so that *usually* feels very normal. This case is an odd one though, because of the magic 5 second timer. Can you give a real use case example for that, so I can think about the mechanics of what I'd expect to happen? **Weirdness #5** This is definitely the `display:none` problem. In this case, the first popover is a `hint`, and the second is an `auto`. While you've *DOM-nested* the `auto` inside the `hint`, they are *unrelated*, according to [how popovers relate to one another](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#topmost-popover-ancestor). That means that when you open the `auto`, it closes the `hint`. That's correct, I think, and is what we want. The "weirdness" you mention here is that because of the DOM-nesting, when the `hint` is closed, it is `display:none`, and its entire subtree becomes invisible. The `auto` is still "open" in the popover sense, you just can't see it. Attaching some `beforetoggle` listeners verifies this. Also, [your flat version example](https://random-stuff.jakearchibald.com/popover-hint-flat/) behaves differently and perhaps more correctly here. **Summary:** Weirdness 1: hints can be "nested" inside an auto. In this case, they work a lot like another auto. Weirdness 2: hints can be "nested" inside an auto. In this case, they work like another auto, and interact differently with other "independent" hints. Weirdness 3: hints are in some sense "on top" of autos, so interacting with them does not light dismiss autos. Weirdness 4: hints are in some sense "on top" of autos, so closing an auto that is "lower" in the stack closes everything above that point in the stack. Weirdness 5: `display:none` hides its entire sub-tree. In my original API design, hints were entirely separate and not nestable within the auto stack. In fact, you were only allowed a single `hint` to be open anywhere on the page. I was talked out of that by the group. Having said that, I do think it's "good" that we allowed hints to be nested within other hints, since there are real world examples that are quite common (see [this example](https://open-ui.org/components/interest-invokers.explainer/#wikipedia-example)). But perhaps allowing a hint to reside in the auto stack was the mistake. That part is the direct cause of #1 and #2, and perhaps to some degree #4. I'm open to changing some of the behaviors to address some of these weirdnesses, if we can agree on the most minimal version of the changes. My concern is compat. This design is several years old, it has been shipped for over a year in Chromium, and there is non-trivial usage of these APIs. But let's first agree on the problems before moving on to [engineering the changes](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/12304#issuecomment-4120000430).

I'll go through these in detail tomorrow, but like I said, weirdness 5 is not a display:none issue, as it exists here too https://random-stuff.jakearchibald.com/popover-hint-flat/ (although slightly different)

> I'll go through these in detail tomorrow, but like I said, weirdness 5 is not a display:none issue, as it exists here too https://random-stuff.jakearchibald.com/popover-hint-flat/ (although slightly different)

The "slightly different" makes all the difference though. Most of the original weirdness was that when you re-showed the hint, the auto magically re-appeared (because of display:none). In the flat demo, the only remaining weirdness is that showing the auto hides the hint, even though they're DOM-nested. So you "think" they should be nested, because you've DOM-nested them, until you realize that autos can't be nested inside hints, making them independent.

And hint 2 and 3 are tooltips related to some content within one of the options, perhaps explaining more detail about the full name or email address in an email address picker, for example. Showing one of them closes the other, quite naturally. And let's say hint 4 is a tooltip for an unrelated item somewhere else on the page, perhaps a tooltip on the "send email" button. Hovering to show that unrelated tooltip shouldn't close either the (auto) picker or the (hint) tooltip on the picker.

To take this example, okay fair enough but why should hovering an option close the unrelated tooltip on the send email button? If it's unrelated it should be completely separate imo.

Sure, but we could also trade weird use-cases for a while. It's good to build a feature based on use-cases, but it's more important to end up with a cohesive feature design. A feature that meets a set of use-cases, but results in a Frankenstein of behaviors, as is the case here, becomes impossible for developers to reason about, so they can't use it for the use-cases it was designed for, because it doesn't feel reliable. As a web developer, and someone who explains features to other web developers, I set out to try and explain `popover=hint`, and I simply couldn't. As I dug further, I encountered more and more inexplicable behaviors. I'm not confident that the 5 I've discovered are the only ones. There are probably more. I'll give use-cases to show why the weirdnesses are weird, but the most important thing is to create a model that makes sense. For weirdness 1, let's say I've created a component that has: - A select button that launches an `auto` picker. - A ℹ️ icon that, on hover, shows a `hint` tooltip about the select button. (we created components like this at Shopify) I receive a bug report saying "can you revert the recent change so hovering the ℹ️ doesn't close the select picker? We've seen users accidentally hover it, and it's annoying that it also closes the picker". This is confusing to me, because what they're describing isn't what I intended, and it isn't what's happening in my automated tests. In my tests, if you open the picker, then hover the ℹ️, the picker stays open, and the tooltip shows. I'm doubly confused, because I haven't updated my component in months, so I'm not sure what change they're referring to. After an extended and frustrating period of debugging, I discover that the reporter of the issue is using my component in their expandable "side bar". Their "side bar" is another component, developed by someone else. The owner of that component recently modernized their implementation to use `popover=auto` for the side bar, and for some reason this completely changes the relationship between the select button picker and tooltip in _my_ component. It blows my mind that my carefully designed component would start behaving in a broken way simply because it's used in a popover "side bar". Fixing 3 & 4 depends on knowing which `auto` popover is the `hint` stack's parent (`hintStackParent`), or `null` if it's separate. As in:

- A `hint` was clicked: All `auto`s are hidden until you get to the `hintStackParent` (which means hiding all `auto`s if `hintStackParent` is null.
- An `auto` was hidden: If the `hintStackParent` is hidden (because it's the `auto` popover we're hiding, or a child `auto` of it), then hide all the `hint`s. Otherwise they remain.
